section_summary: This section traces the formation of conservative teachers’ unions in Tokyo and their federation in opposition to the Zenkyo. It describes the Ministry of Education’s unsuccessful attempt to unite teachers under nonradical leadership, the Zenkyo’s political campaign, and the spread of teachers’ unions across Japan.

subfiles.title: A History of Teachers’ Unions in Japan
subfiles.about: The report examines competing teachers’ unions and their expansion in postwar Japan.
subfiles.summary: The Seikyo, Chukyo, and Kokkyo emerged as conservative alternatives to the Zenkyo and formed a Tokyo federation in April 1946. The Ministry of Education’s effort to bring independent unions together failed after a Zenkyo delegate challenged its involvement. The report then describes the Zenkyo’s political arguments and campaign against its opponents, followed by the growth of prefectural unions and uncertainty about how widely members shared the Zenkyo’s aims.
